issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s default statutory ability to sublet does not prevent eviction under rent-control legislation when the tenant sublets without the landlord’s consent and the lease does not grant a right to sublet.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction under rent-control legislation on the ground that the tenant had sublet the premises without the landlord’s consent.
The tenant relied on the default right to sublet under the general property law, but the right had not been granted by the lease or by the landlord’s subsequent consent.
The eviction order was affirmed by the courts below.
issues.conclusion: Subletting without the landlord’s consent is a ground for eviction where the lease does not grant a right to sublet; the default right under general property law is no defence. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11(4)(i) of the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965 makes subletting a ground for eviction unless the lease grants the right or the landlord subsequently consents. The right under section 108(j) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 cannot be claimed unilaterally and is displaced to the extent that the rent-control statute provides a specific ground for eviction. The Court relied on V. Dhanapal Chettiar v. Yesodai Ammal, AIR 1979 SC 1745, for the principle that State Rent Acts may displace rights under section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act where the matter is provided for expressly or by necessary implication.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and tenant_sublet and not landlord_consented and not lease_granted_subletting_right

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction under rent-control legislation.
predicates.tenant_sublet: The tenant transferred or sublet the premises or part of it to another person.
predicates.landlord_consented: The landlord agreed to the subletting, either through the lease or subsequently.
predicates.lease_granted_subletting_right: The lease granted the tenant a right to sublet.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding under rent-control legislation concerns a tenant’s subletting, and neither the landlord’s consent nor a right granted by the lease authorizes it, the subletting is an eviction ground.
